[verdict]
In the 50 retrieved episodes where the tape looked like this, the realised 5-session returns for QQQ had a median of -0.48% and a standard deviation of 2.45%. When you specifically condition on a +2 sigma VIX spike, the historical median forward return over five sessions was -0.18%, with a 10th percentile of -5.26%. The path gets uncomfortable but rarely un-holdable: in 96% of those volatility-shock analogs, the position stayed within a 10% drawdown.

[state]
The engine pulled these 50 analogs because the current state is defined by thin liquidity meeting rising energy costs against a low-volatility backdrop. The most distinctive feature is the 20-session dollar-volume regime z-score (dv20z) at -2.262, which translates to a z-score of -1.396, indicating unusually quiet volume. WTI crude change over 20 days (oilChg20) is up 19.24% (z = 1.124), while 20-session realised volatility (vol20) sits at only 13.24% (z = -0.8). The 5d/20d volatility ratio (volRatio) is elevated at 1.236 (z = 0.825), showing recent choppiness despite the low absolute vol. QQQ is trading at 721.45, sitting -3.63% from its 52-week high (dist52, z = 0.725) and -2.03% from its 60-session peak (dd60, z = 0.649). These features collectively pull in historical sessions characterised by illiquid drifts punctuated by sudden energy-driven repricings.

[history]
Across the 50 analogs spanning 2016-12-14 to 2026-09-08, the mean 5-session return was -0.09% and the median was -0.48%. The distribution is slightly positively skewed (skew = 0.33), with a 10th percentile of -2.98% and a 90th percentile of 3.48%. Returns finished below zero in 56% of the episodes. The bad tail is dominated by specific recent sessions: Morgan Stanley (MS) on 2026-09-04 returned -5.12% with a max adverse excursion of -5.93%; Procter & Gamble (PG) on 2026-09-02 returned -3.16%; and IWM on 2026-09-08 returned -2.98%. Conversely, QQQ itself on 2025-06-20 returned 4.15%, showing that upside outliers exist in this regime. The closest analog by distance (0.3066) is QQQ on 2026-09-08, which went on to lose -1.92% over the next five sessions.

[tails]
A trade can end near flat and still be un-holdable if the intra-week path swings violently. In this analog set, the median max adverse excursion was -1.35%. At the 25th percentile, the adverse excursion reached -2.42%, and at the 10th percentile it hit -3.7%. The median max favourable excursion was 1.15%, yielding a reward-to-risk ratio of 0.85. Looking at hard drawdown thresholds, the probability of breaching a 5% drawdown during the 5-session horizon was 6%. No analog in the retrieved set breached a 10%, 15%, or 20% drawdown threshold. The conformal interval, scaled to target 80% coverage, spans from -3.69% to 2.73%, a total width of 6.42%.

[stress]
You asked about a two-sigma volatility spike. The "vol-spike" scenario directly conditions on a +2 sigma VIX shock. Across 50 analogs, the median 5-session return was -0.18%, which is actually 0.3% better than the baseline median of -0.48%. However, the 10th percentile drops to -5.26%, and the median max adverse excursion is -1.05%. The probability of breaching a 10% drawdown is 4%, meaning 96% of the time the position held within that band. The caveat here is critical: VIX shocks mean-revert quickly, so this stresses entry timing more than terminal value.

If that vol spike coincides with a systemic liquidity failure, the "covid-crash" scenario shows what happens. Across 48 analogs, the median return plunges to -3.3% (a delta of -2.82% versus baseline), the 10th percentile hits -11.99%, and the probability of breaching a 10% drawdown jumps to 50%. The caveat is that central-bank backstops arrived inside the window, so the realised rebound is baked into the forward returns; it is a sample of one regime, not a forecast of the next one.

The "tariff-shock-2025" scenario also worsens the picture materially. Across 26 analogs, the median is -0.68%, but the 10th percentile is -11.8%, and the probability of breaching a 10% drawdown is 26.9%. The caveat is that policy reversals inside the window make the tail of the distribution asymmetric in a way that is specific to that episode.

The "carry-unwind-2024" scenario produced a median return of -0.39% across 36 analogs, with an 8.3% probability of breaching a 10% drawdown. The caveat is that the reversal was almost as fast as the drawdown, so H-day forward returns look benign even though the intra-horizon excursion did not.

Scenarios like "regional-banks-2023", "rates-up", "liquidity-air-pocket", "crypto-contagion", and "china-adr-shock" all produced median returns that were equal to or better than the baseline, meaning they do not worsen the picture for this specific query. None of the 14 scenarios run were skipped.

[reasoning]
The three scenarios most relevant to your question are: first, "vol-spike", because it directly answers your +2 sigma VIX premise, showing a median of -0.18% across 50 analogs with only a 4% chance of a 10% breach; second, "covid-crash", because if a vol spike triggers forced deleveraging, the median drops to -3.3% (delta -2.82%) and the 10% breach probability hits 50% across 48 analogs; third, "tariff-shock-2025", because it represents a discrete policy shock where the 10th percentile reaches -11.8% and the 10% breach probability is 26.9% across 26 analogs. You should distrust the heavy concentration of 2025 (22 analogs) and 2026 (17 analogs) in the retrieval set, which means the distribution is overwhelmingly shaped by very recent market microstructure rather than diverse historical regimes. No scenario contradicts the direction of your idea; even the vol-spike scenario yields a negative median, confirming downside skew when volatility re-prices.

[limits]
This analysis has concrete limits. The honest verdict from the engine's validation is: Analog retrieval hits its coverage target out of sample and its width tracks each instrument's own volatility, but it is NOT sharper than a same-name unconditional band at matched coverage, and its raw PIT distribution fails a uniformity test. It is a stress-testing and provenance instrument, not an alpha source. The directional hit rate is only 50.1%.

Regarding path risk, the engine predicts a 10% drawdown breach probability based on the analog share, but out-of-sample testing over 2698 queries shows the mean predicted breach rate was 3.4% while the realised breach rate was only 2%. This yields a calibration gap of 1.4 percentage points, with a clustered standard error of 0.48. The analog Brier score (MAE) is 0.0196. Paired differences show the analog beats the volatility reflection benchmark (Brier 0.0241, delta -0.0045, CI95 [-0.0071, -0.0022]), the same-name calibration (Brier 0.024, delta -0.0045, CI95 [-0.0059, -0.0029]), and the pooled calibration (Brier 0.021, delta -0.0014, CI95 [-0.0023, -0.0005]). Because none of these confidence intervals span zero, the paired Brier comparisons are resolved in favour of the analog model, even though the model systematically overstates the breach frequency.

Finally, if you hold this via a tokenised wrapper, the status is measured on Bitget official MCP (QQQ/USDT, an RWA perpetual). The reference cash market is shut for 81.4% of the week, yet 62.09% of the wrapper's own hourly price movement lands in those closed hours. It is a fair tracker with a return correlation of 0.9426 and a tracking error of 43 bp/day. The basis band is -0.11% to 0.48%, and the spread is 0.13 bps. The caveat is that a fair perpetual is not the underlying; it carries idiosyncratic risk and funding. Across 6 observed weekend blocks, the median weekend return was -0.0665%, the 10th percentile was -1.1155%, the standard deviation was 0.8798%, and the median intra-weekend adverse excursion was -0.5825%. Zero percent of those specific weekend blocks breached a 5% drawdown. These are wrapper returns measured while the reference market was shut and are NOT the retrieved outcome distribution above, which is built on 5x24 daily sessions of the underlying.
